source_title: India slams global energy disruptions through sanctions, chokepoints
source_excerpt: Washington External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar strongly disapproved of disruptions in global oil supplies through sanctions and chokepoints, saying deliberate attacks on energy trade and infrastructure were a calculated strategy to hold prices hostage. Mr. Jaishankar’s remarks at the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Atlanta on Friday (October 30, 2026) came amid American sanctions on the sale of Iranian oil and disruption to energy supplies from West Asia and the decision to lift sanctions on the sale of Russian diesel. https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/marco-rubio-hosts-g20-foreign-ministers-as-iran-ukraine-wars-divide-members/article71643995.ece Jaishankar hits out at U.S. tariffs, says India will not compromise on farmers' interests Jaishankar hits out at U.S. tariffs, says India will not compromise on farmers' interests The Minister argued that the tariff issue was being wrongly presented as an “oil dispute” Jaishankar hits out at U.S. tariffs, says India will not compromise on farmers' interests storyline 1 The Minister said that the world was staring at an energy crisis not of production, but of unpredictability and disruption, unaffordable costs, and challenges of access. Mr. Jaishankar, in a post on X, said he highlighted that deliberate attacks on energy trade and infrastructure were a calculated strategy to hold energy prices hostage. “The G20 must display both understanding and leadership to keep energy markets open and predictable,” he said at the meeting convened by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Mr. Jaishankar said he underscored that there appears to be little regard for the predicament of low-income countries.
